description: Hi,We are Terra Bytes, participants in the Nasa Space Apps Challenge.We are a young duo interested in science, technology and understanding the world around us. Our project explores the Urban Heat Island effect in Gauteng using NASA POWER data. We chose Gauteng because, as a beginners, we wanted to start with a familiar environment before exploring global climate trends. We're excited to learn, challenge ourselves and discover how data and technology can help us understand environmental issues.
summary:
Gauteng Urban Heat Island Detective (2001-2025) by Terra Byte

This project answers the challenge: Be an Earth System Trend Detective! This project investigates term trends in temperature and climate data from two different areas: urban areas (Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni) and rural control area (Highveld grasslands).

Utilising NASA POWER data that combines data from satellites and MERRA-2 reanalysis we have analysed data from 2001-2025. We have created a dashboard using HTML5 and Chart.js to display key climate trends such as average air temperature, minimum air temperature, Earth skin temperature and rainfall. We have also implemented filtering for missing data values (shown as -999) as well as taking into account changes in elevation.

This project investigates how urban developments, land cover changes and other factors can affect the difference in trends between rural areas.We have looked at how temperatures change at night to help identify how urban areas are different to areas.

By simplifying the data from Earth observation Team Terra Byte have aimed to help show long term climate trends. We have shown how NASA Earth data can be used to increase awareness around the environment encouraging evidence based urban planning.We have shown how green infrastructure and climate resilience can be discussed with reference to the data.

We want to demonstrate how Earth observation data from around the world can help us understand changes in the environment, within our communities
details:
An interactive HTML5/Chart.js dashboard analyzing 25-years(2001 to 2025) of NASA POWER (MERRA-2) satellite data to compare urban heat in Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni against a rural Highveld grass land control

Impact:Tracks multi-dimensional thermal indicators sentimental filtering and lapse-rate correction providing urban planners with a scalable blueprint for green-infrastructure cooling

Factors considered:

•Urban vs Rural pairing

•Tracking multiple metrics

•Cleaning data

•Scientific honesty

•Making it reusable

We believe our project is creative because it includes:

●Interactive storytelling: Turning 25 years of NASA data into an explorable web dashboard where judges can toggle between urban,rural and heat delta views

●Global blueprint: Designing a lightweight backend-free stack that any city planner worldwide can easily adapt for their own region

●Building an open methodology modal right into the tool that exposes our data filtering and elevation math.

●Pairing Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni against a rural grassland baseline to pinpoint real human-made heat divergence
